title: GPUSparse: GPU-Accelerated Learned Sparse Retrieval with Parallel Inverted Indices
event_hint: arXiv paper published 2026-06-24 on GPU-accelerated exact learned sparse retrieval using parallel inverted indices
problem: Learned sparse retrieval models (SPLADE) achieve quality competitive with dense models while preserving interpretability, but inference-time scoring relies on CPU-bound inverted index traversal algorithms (WAND, Block-Max WAND). This creates a fundamental bottleneck for real-time serving at scale. Existing GPU sparse retrieval systems (Seismic) trade 25% recall for speed.
mechanism: GPUSparse introduces: (1) GPU-parallel inverted index with block-aligned, warp-coalesced posting lists, (2) batched scatter-add scoring algorithm processing hundreds of queries simultaneously, (3) fused Triton kernels. The scatter-add kernel processes only O(q_bar * L_bar) entries per query (query terms × posting lists). A document-parallel kernel trades work-efficiency for bandwidth utilization.

evidence.claim: 235x speedup over Pyserini CPU exact scoring at 8.8M documents
evidence.condition: MS MARCO passage ranking 8.8M passages, batch 500, H100 80GB

evidence.claim: Achieves 787 QPS throughput at 8.8M documents with batch 500
evidence.condition: MS MARCO 8.8M passages, batch 500, H100 80GB, exact scoring

evidence.claim: Document-parallel kernel achieves 62.6% of H100 peak HBM bandwidth
Scatter-add kernel achieves 12.5 GB/s effective bandwidth (0.37% of peak) due to scattered atomic writes
8.5 GB for inverted index at 8.8M passages (11% of 80GB H100)

evaluation_context: Evaluated on MS MARCO passage ranking (8.8M passages) with real SPLADE embeddings. Hardware: H100 80GB GPU. Metrics include MRR@10, Recall@1000, per-query latency, QPS throughput. Cross-domain validation on BEIR benchmarks (SciFact, NFCorpus, TREC-COVID). Comparison against Pyserini CPU exact scoring, Seismic (fastest CPU sparse), cuSPARSE SpMV, and dense matmul ground truth.
limitations: GPU cost: H100 GPU is substantially more expensive than CPU-only retrieval. Single-query latency 9.6ms at 8.8M docs - CPU methods faster for single-query approximate search. Score buffer memory scales as O(B*N): 44GB at batch 500 with 8.8M docs (55% of H100). No dynamic updates without full index rebuild. 6x slower than Seismic for approximate top-10 retrieval at 8.8M.
project_relevance: GPUSparse demonstrates memory-bandwidth-bound sparse retrieval on H100 with 62.6% peak utilization achieved via document-parallel kernel. The work-efficiency vs bandwidth-efficiency tradeoff is fundamental: scatter-add processes only query-relevant postings (work-efficient) at 0.37% bandwidth utilization, while doc-parallel achieves 62.6% peak but reads 76GB vs 0.09GB per batch. The 8.5GB index size at 8.8M passages shows sparse format memory advantage vs dense (~1TB). Index cannot be updated without full rebuild - limitation for dynamic workloads.
